label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is TP because user-controlled header names flow to the HTML sink via 'param'/'bar'/'input', and per policy, attacker-controlled data reaching the sink overrides encoding-based mitigation claims. Alert 2 (java/stack-trace-exposure) is TP because 'e.printStackTrace(response.getWriter())' exposes server-side exceptions to the client. Alert 3 (java/weak-cryptographic-algorithm) is FP because the algorithm string is sourced from a static resource ('benchmark.properties') or a compile-time default literal, not user input.

evidence.note: Alert 1: Request header names (user-controlled) flow through 'param'/'bar' to 'input' and finally to 'encodeForHTML' sink at L114-120. Data remains attacker-controlled.
Alert 2: 'e.printStackTrace(response.getWriter())' writes stack trace to response, exposing internal errors.
Alert 3: Algorithm determined by 'benchmark.properties' or default literal 'AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding', not user input.
